gloss: roughly; more or less; once through

definitions.gloss: roughly; more or less; in general
definitions.explanation: Indicates doing something to a basic or general degree without going into great depth or detail.

definitions.gloss: once through; from beginning to end
definitions.explanation: Indicates going through something completely once, covering all items or steps.

examples.japanese: {一通|ひととお}り{説明|せつめい}した。
{料理|りょうり}は{一通|ひととお}りできる。
examples.english: I can do most types of cooking.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{文法|ぶんぽう}は{一通|ひととお}り{勉強|べんきょう}したが、まだ{自信|じしん}がない。
examples.english: I've studied Japanese grammar more or less, but I'm still not confident.

examples.japanese: {資料|しりょう}に{一通|ひととお}り{目|め}を{通|とお}した。
examples.english: I looked through the materials once.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{議題|ぎだい}を{一通|ひととお}り{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked through all the meeting agenda items.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}に{仕事|しごと}の{流|なが}れを{一通|ひととお}り{教|おし}えてから、{実践|じっせん}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: After teaching the new employee the workflow from start to finish, we moved on to practice.

notes:
An extremely common adverb meaning to do something to a general degree or to go through something once completely. The two senses overlap — both involve covering something without exhaustive depth.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一通|ひととお}り{目|め}を{通|とお}す: to look through (a document) once
- {一通|ひととお}り{説明|せつめい}する: to explain roughly
- {一通|ひととお}りできる: to be able to do (something) more or less
- {一通|ひととお}り{終|お}わる: to finish going through everything
- {一通|ひととお}り{揃|そろ}う: to have a basic set of everything

USAGE:
Sense 1 often appears with verbs of ability ({一通|ひととお}りできる) to indicate general competence. Sense 2 often pairs with verbs of checking or reviewing to indicate covering all items.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ざっと: more casual; emphasizes speed and roughness
- だいたい: focuses on approximation rather than coverage
- ひと{通|とお}り: same word, alternate kanji rendering
